newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS -- The four leading contenders to become the first Chief Executive of the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government were all confident of being selected as candidates today.

-- MING PAO DAILY -- The government will take top security measures to protect Chinese vice-premier Qian Qichen when he arrives in Hong Kong to chair the meeting of the Selection Committee which will name nominees for Chief Executive.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Members of the Democratic Party held an overnight protest against the refusal of Chinese vice-premier Qian Qichen to meet their colleagues.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin told a delegation of U.S. senators that China pays high attention to Sino-U.S. relations.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- After Glorious Sun Enterprises, which is involved in the Chinese garment business, received a positive response to its share flotation, several companies with similar businesses are considering listing.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chinese power minister Zhi Dazhen said that China would invest 700 billion yuan in the next five years to boost its electricity output.
-- European credit rating agency IBCA reaffirmed Hong Kong's A-plus long-term foreign currency debt rating, expressing its confidence in a smooth transition next July.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa is entering the home stretch of the race for Chief Executive as the hot favourite, with at least 160 of 400 votes in his pocket.
